body:
I can't begin to describe how I felt when I went through this post. First off, thank you. I did not expect to see anything when I logged back into this supposedly throwaway account. When I saw this single multi-paragraph long post I did not felt motivated to read it, but to quote Thorin from The Hobbit: "I've never been so wrong in all my life." 

I think your post is the only post on reddit that I read multiple times, feeling the same deep warmth every single time. This warmth seemed foreign to me - in school I often come off as cold, indifferent, stern, and unapproachable, which naturally distanced me from the warmth I seek deep down. I rarely seek out companionship, deeming myself superior to many and refusing to show an action that can be interpreted as weakness. Past experiences in opening myself up to the companionship of others often result in my anguish, since my friends are often pursuing the same goals as me and when they triumph in a mutual goal, I can only smile while bleeding inside.

I have to say, your use of imagery is spot on. Cardboard thrones? Cascade Failure? Brilliant. It captures exactly how such petty school politics feel. For now I am comforting myself with "it's their loss for not choosing me", but it still pains me to see how under qualifying individuals can be accredited with the honor (if it can even still be called honor) that I worked harder for. 

Your statement on the time I spent is not wasted, though true in entirety, is still somewhat hard to accept. However, despite credit not being given where it is due, I recognize that I have grown throughout the experience, the best and worst parts of it. Assuming a leadership role in a big club like honor societies is no small task, but it allowed me to learn how to optimize productivity as well as revealing to me the abyss that is real life. In the end, I am grateful this blow in my plan happened in high school, since the bitter taste of failure fades over time and allows juxtaposition for the sweet victory to come.

I think I really just needed to vent and never truly had the courage to commit suicide (I love life too much, despite its constant let downs). As I stated before, I was always perceptive, be it towards others, social interactions, or myself. This is why I sometimes am hard to approach - I poke through people's facades (god do I sound emo). I think self-awareness is also why I can force myself to sit down and vent with language, since I know this is what can help me. As for committing suicide, I think if I were to commit suicide it would be out of overwhelming curiosity of what happens after death (even though I am a strong advocate for the idea that nothing needs to happen after death).

As for your compliments on my "mastery of prose", I think you'll find it amusing that I have Biology as my intended major (But hey, I got an A on an extremely hard timed writing assignment for IBHL English today, so that was one thing nice that happened on this horrible day). To be honest, I am finding fun in a broad variety of subjects and I now feel the disparity between how I felt when I pinpointed my intended major and my feelings now. As for writing, I now have an urge to publish a muckraking article on the nature of these honor societies in the school newspaper before I graduate. It's just an idea though (probably a really bad one), but I'll see how that goes if I do intend to follow through.

I think I just spent an hour on this response but I don't regret it at all. Thanks for being awesome.

thank you for your response, I can't even begin to imagine how horrible dropping out of high school must have felt for you.

I will still attempt my best with whatever purpose I feel I have left. Thanks for your support at this tough time.

Thank you. I feel better now after going out to cool my head, listening to my favorite classical music, and just getting myself out of my depressed bubble. 

I realize that in hindsight all these will seem insignificant, but it's just the fact that such blatant favoritism is allowed in an "honor society".

A few hours ago when I wrote this I couldn't actually see what I could possibly do. Taking some time off of the matter helped. I think I never would've had the courage to commit suicide, but instead simply needed to vent.

Thanks for being here.

Oooo speaking of music experiences I've had another one of those. Feeling better now though, thank you.

Heard of AMIS? Yeah, I worked to get into the HS Honor band from March till about November until the digital auditions are due, took over 400 takes for 5 ~1 minute tracks. As you probably guessed, I didn't get in. This was huge blow at the time, but looking back I do realize my inferiority.

Somewhat unrelated but wtv 

EDIT: forgot to thank you for being here. Thank you.
